name: labeled-group
title: Labeled Group
description: A Block Region with only a title: a thin frame and a title card in its top-left corner, square where the card meets the frame. React Flow UI's Labeled Group Node, as a preset.

import type { CSSProperties, ReactNode } from "react"; import { cn } from "../lib/utils"; import { DEFAULT_HIGHLIGHTER_KIND, DiagnosticFlag, DIAGNOSTIC_FLAG_SIZE_PX, diagnosticColorVar, highlighterMaskFrameStyle, highlighterStrokeOutlineStyle, maxDiagnosticSeverity, type Diagnostic, type HighlighterKind, } from "./highlighter"; import { HIT_REGION_FILL, HIT_REGION_OUTLINE } from "./hitRegion"; import { BLOCK_MEMBER_GAP_PX, BLOCK_MEMBER_INSET_PX, BlockMembers, type BlockInsetBackground, type BlockMember, type BlockMembersLayout, } from "./blockMembers"; import { BlockDescription, blockDescriptionIsPainted } from "./blockDescription"; import type { ReorderChord } from "./keyboardReorder"; import { ISOLATED_ROOT_STYLE, paintTier } from "./paintOrder"; /** * Block — header / body / footer, stacked. All three are plain slots: pass * text, pass nothing, or pass a to compose the two components * together (that composition is the point of this reset pass — see * src/components/Block.stories.tsx's "ComposedWithBar" story). A slot given * `undefined` is omitted entirely, not merely emptied, so a header-less * Block draws no stray divider line. Painted with Tailwind + the shadcn CSS * variables from src/globals.css. * * WHY this file imports no port concept, and must keep not doing so (Zach, * 2026-09-17, docs/BLOCK-PORT-EDGES-PLAN.md D-A1): Block is usable on its * own — a card with a header, a body, a footer — and ports are something * "we're starting to add more and more things to", not a fact about every * Block. `./blockPort.tsx`'s `BlockPort` is the wrapper that mounts ports on * a Block's walls; it composes THIS component from the outside rather than * this component growing port props, because Block's own root below is * `overflow-hidden` and would clip a rail dot that deliberately straddles * the border line. See blockPort.tsx's own header for the reciprocal note. * * WHY `body` is conditional like the other two, and `height` has no default: * Zach's folding-chevron requirement is "make sure that it hides the body and * footer when you click it." Body used to render unconditionally and `height` * defaulted to 240, so a collapsed Block stayed a 240px box with an empty * well under its header — the text vanished but nothing folded (measured: * 180px open, 180px closed, body GREW 80px → 125px as the footer left). Both * halves are needed: omitting the region is what removes the content, and an * absent height is what lets the box hug what remains. That also restores * this repo's own stated size contract (ARCHITECTURE.md): "Explicit size when * the scene carries one; hug contents when it does not" — a caller that wants * a fixed box still passes one. * * WHY the header/footer wrappers' `px-3 py-2` is cancelled with * `has-[>[data-slot=bar]]:p-0` rather than removed outright: Zach's bar * feedback wants a Bar filling the header/footer to sit edge-to-edge with * the divider — a Bar's OWN `px-3` (bar.tsx) supplies the inset instead, so * stacking both paddings would double it back up. A bare string/ReactNode * header (no Bar) still needs Block's own padding — it has none of its own * — so the wrapper keeps `px-3 py-2` as its default and only zeroes it when * a `` is the direct child, detected via `data-slot="bar"` rather than * a new Block prop. */ /** * The outline a Block draws — its four corner radii, and nothing else. * * - `"card"` (default): rounded at all four corners with the skin radius, the * Block every caller has always had. * - `"region-corner"`: the Block sitting in a `BlockRegion`'s top-left corner. * Rounded with the region FRAME's radius at the top-left, the corner it * shares with the frame, and at its one free corner, the bottom-right. * SQUARE at the top-right and bottom-left. * * WHY top-right and bottom-left are square: those two are the JUNCTIONS. The * card's top edge continues as the frame's top rule, and its left edge as the * frame's left rule. A radius there pulls the card's edge away from the * frame's line, so the border kinks twice on its way round. Zach, 2026-09-19, * annotating the tldraw app (`Pasted image 20260919180659.png`): "I don't * like how the edges where it meets the region are still curve. they shuld be * straight!" WHAT THIS REJECTS: the all-round `card`, the tempting default * because every other Block on the board wears it. It makes the corner read * as a card PARKED in the frame rather than part of it. Squaring all four * was rejected too: the top-left is the frame's own corner (they curve * together, so there is no junction to break) and the bottom-right touches no * frame edge, and the drawing he approved rounds both. * * WHY a Block prop and not a rule inside `BlockRegion` (Zach, 2026-09-22: * "the block region styling we apply to the block like corning the corners. * that is just a styling change to Block"): a canvas host may mount the corner * card as an INDEPENDENT element. `apps/systemsketch` paints it as a real * `ss-block` child shape, so it is not a React descendant of the region and no * CSS rule the region writes can reach it. It is a fact about the card's own * outline, so it travels with the card. It used to be an exported style object * every host had to remember to spread (`REGION_CORNER_BLOCK_STYLE`), and a * `BlockRegion` story that forgot it shipped the all-round card (2026-09-22). * A named shape is harder to forget than an object to spread. */ export type BlockShape = "card" | "region-corner"; /** The card radius, the value every Block wore before `shape` existed. */ const CARD_RADIUS = "var(--bbox-skin-radius, var(--radius-lg))"; /** * The region frame's shared top-left radius. `BlockRegion`'s frame reads this * same chain, and a `region-corner` Block curves with it. `v1` resolves to the * skin radius. A region drawing (`skin/regionVariants.css`) sets * `--bbox-region-frame-radius` on an ancestor, and the frame and its corner * card both follow, because both read this one string. */ export const REGION_FRAME_RADIUS = "var(--bbox-region-frame-radius, var(--bbox-skin-radius, var(--radius-lg)))"; type CornerRadii = { tl: string; tr: string; br: string; bl: string }; const SHAPE_RADII: Record = { card: { tl: CARD_RADIUS, tr: CARD_RADIUS, br: CARD_RADIUS, bl: CARD_RADIUS }, "region-corner": { tl: REGION_FRAME_RADIUS, tr: "0px", // The one free corner follows the drawing: `v2` and `v10` square it so // a full-width header rule leaves the card cleanly instead of from a curve. br: `var(--bbox-region-corner-radius, ${REGION_FRAME_RADIUS})`, bl: "0px", }, }; /** `border-radius` for a shape, optionally grown by `growPx` at every corner * (the mask highlighter's Minkowski offset). A card's four equal corners stay * the single value they always were, so a card's inline style is unchanged. */ function shapeRadiusCss(shape: BlockShape, growPx = 0): string { const r = SHAPE_RADII[shape]; const grow = (value: string) => (growPx ? `calc(${value} + ${growPx}px)` : value); if (r.tl === r.tr && r.tr === r.br && r.br === r.bl) return grow(r.tl); return [r.tl, r.tr, r.br, r.bl].map(grow).join(" "); } export interface BlockProps { header?: ReactNode; body?: ReactNode; footer?: ReactNode; width?: number; /** Explicit height in px. Omit to hug the rendered regions. */ height?: number; /** The outline: `"card"` (default) or `"region-corner"`. See `BlockShape`. */ shape?: BlockShape; style?: CSSProperties; /** * The divider line under the header. Defaults to shown, so no existing * caller changes. WHY a prop and not a className override: SystemSketch's * own Block chrome treats "Header divider: Show|Hide" as a first-class * toggle beside "Footer: Show|Hide" (blockModel.ts's * `BlockShowHeaderDividerStyle`) — a header-only card (Zach's minimal * "Attributes" variant) wants the title to sit directly on the body with * no line between. Footer hiding needs no prop: omit `footer` and the * region is omitted entirely (the existing contract). */ showHeaderDivider?: boolean; /** * How wide the header band is. `"full"` (default) spans the block — the * header every Block has always had. `"hug"` shrink-wraps its content: * the HEAD TAB. Zach, 2026-09-22, sketching a Block with its header * shrunk to a tab (`Pasted image 20260922184414.png`, "Head Tab View"): * the tab's bottom edge continues as the body's top rule, and its right * edge closes the tab off — an L, not the full-width single rule a * `"full"` header draws. `showHeaderDivider={false}` still means NO * rules at all in either fit (`Pasted image 20260922184423.png`, * "Hidding header lines": a bare chevron, title and port dot, no * outline) — `showHeaderDivider` alone still gates whether anything * paints; `headerFit` only changes WHICH sides paint when it does. * * `blockPort.tsx`'s `useBlockBands` measures the tab's own right edge * (`headerRight`) off this element's rendered width — `w-fit` + * `self-start` below is what gives it one narrower than the block to * measure, rather than `railBoxFor` needing a second, computed source * of truth for the same line. */ headerFit?: "full" | "hug"; /** * The divider line above the footer — `showHeaderDivider`'s missing * sibling. Block used to have no way to hide it at all: the footer * wrapper's `border-t` was unconditional, unlike the header's own * `showHeaderDivider && "border-b…"` gate two lines below. Added * alongside `editor/contextMenuModel.ts`'s `buildBlockMenu` ("Hide * Footer Line" is one of Zach's nine right-click commands, and it needs * a real prop to flip, the same way "Hide Header Line" already had one) * — defaults to shown, so no existing caller changes. */ showFooterDivider?: boolean; /** * The sentence under the title. Ported from the frozen v1 lineage — * `packages/bbox-ui/src/blockFace.tsx:437-454` paints it immediately after * the header in both header modes, which is the placement restated here. * * WHY it is a Block prop and not something a caller stuffs into `body`: * v1 governs it as a FIELD (`block.fields.ts`'s `DESCRIPTION_FIELD`) with * its own visibility toggle, so "is there a description, and is it shown" * is a question about the block, answerable without inspecting whatever * ReactNode a host happened to pass. The whiteboard's right-hand inspector * asks exactly that question. */ description?: string; /** * Whether the description paints. Defaults to `true` — the donor field's * own `defaultValue: true` (`block.fields.ts:120-124`), so no existing * caller changes and a newly-typed description is visible immediately. * * WHY a separate boolean rather than clearing `description` to hide it * (Zach, ruling 9 — the control is an EYE, in the right-hand inspector): * an eye hides; it does not delete. Folding the two into one field would * mean toggling visibility off threw the author's text away, and toggling * it back on gave them an empty block. */ showDescription?: boolean; /** * The description region, rendered BY THE HOST instead of by this component. * When present it replaces the whole region — the `

` included — and both * `description` and `showDescription` are then the host's business. * * WHY a host would need this at all: a host that lets a person edit the * description WHERE IT IS PAINTED has to swap the sentence for a control in * this exact spot, between the header and the body, and a `string` prop * cannot carry a control. `header` and `body` already work this way; this is * the same seam for the one region that did not have it. Zach's "edit it in * place, on the card, not in a panel field somewhere else" (P-039/P-026) is * what it is for, and `apps/systemsketch/src/shapes/block/BlockFace.tsx` is * the caller. * * WHY it is additive rather than widening `description` to a `ReactNode`, * which is the obvious move: `description` is a governed FIELD (see its own * doc above) and `blockDescriptionIsPainted` has to be able to ask whether * it is empty. A ReactNode cannot be asked that, so widening the prop would * either drop the gate or make it lie. Every existing caller is byte * -identical, because a caller that passes nothing here takes the branch it * always took. */ descriptionSlot?: ReactNode; /** * Membership — "boxes all the way down". Members render in their own * region between body and footer; `membersLayout` picks how the ONE * member list is laid out (free = a frame inside, stack = an ordered * column). See ./blockMembers.tsx for the vocabulary and its * SystemSketch provenance. */ members?: BlockMember[]; membersLayout?: BlockMembersLayout; /** Enables drag-to-reorder of stacked members, kanban-card style. */ onMembersChange?(members: BlockMember[]): void; /** The IDE move-line chord for stacked members — `BlockMembersProps.reorderChord`. */ membersReorderChord?: ReorderChord; memberGap?: number; memberGutter?: number; insetBackground?: BlockInsetBackground; showMembers?: boolean; showCards?: boolean; /** * The diagnostic axis (docs/INVALID-STATES-PLAN.md §5's Block row, * amended by Zach's report feedback — see `HighlighterKind`'s own doc * in ./highlighter.tsx). `error`/`warning` get a mark in whichever * `highlighterKind` the caller asked for, plus the corner * `DiagnosticFlag`; `info` paints nothing at all, matching §5's * board-scale calm rule. The flag carries a COUNT once the list is * longer than one (`DiagnosticFlag`'s own doc). * * The `"halo"` kind keeps its ORIGINAL, narrower rule — `error` alone, * "warning must not shout" — because a soft ambient glow is genuinely * loud; `"stroke"`/`"mask"` mark both severities uniformly (a crisp * outline does not have the same shouting problem), matching how * JointJS's own highlighters behave. */ diagnostics?: Diagnostic[]; /** Which `HighlighterKind` draws the mark. Defaults to * `DEFAULT_HIGHLIGHTER_KIND` ("stroke") — Zach's own lean from the * report feedback; `"halo"` is the pre-existing treatment, kept as a * sibling, not deleted. */ highlighterKind?: HighlighterKind; /** * Suppress the corner `DiagnosticFlag` while keeping the mark (default * `true` — every existing caller unchanged). `ValueCapsule` * (components/block.value.tsx) is the one caller that sets this `false`: * §5's own words are "no flag — a capsule is too small, the glow is the * beacon and the message rides a hover Tooltip" — the mark is still * this component's, the flag specifically is not. */ showDiagnosticFlag?: boolean; /** * Let `warning` earn the `"halo"` kind's mark too (default `false` — * Block's own row: "warning must not shout"). Only meaningful with * `highlighterKind="halo"` — `"stroke"`/`"mask"` already mark both * severities regardless. `ValueCapsule` sets this `true` for its OWN * row ("warning: amber glow"), because a capsule has no flag at all to * carry warning instead. Block itself never sets this. */ diagnosticWarningGlow?: boolean; /** * Stable string the sketch skin's hand-drawn outline is generated from — * same seed, same wobble, every render (see sketchPath.ts). Defaults to * a size-derived string so two same-sized Blocks don't draw identical * wobble by coincidence of both falling back the same way; pass an id * when two same-sized Blocks need visibly different hand-drawn lines. */ sketchSeed?: string; /** * Paint Block's hit region. Block has NO hit constant — deliberately: as * a DOM element its pointer target is the browser's own hit test, which * stops at the border box exactly (the same "there was no number to * choose" React Flow's DOM nodes have; contrast tldraw's ±3 screen px * `hitTestMargin`). So what this paints IS that fact: a wash over the * border box, nothing outside it. Pure paint — absolutely positioned, * `pointer-events: none`, moves no layout and eats no clicks. */ showHitRegion?: boolean; } /** * The root's own border width, px, used only to size `overflowClipMargin` * below. A literal, not `--bbox-skin-stroke-width` read back out of CSS: * this app carries no wall-anchor geometry that needs the two to be the * SAME variable (donor's block.tsx / skin.css both flag that trap — see * skin.css's own port-of-omission note), so a plain constant is honest * here. It still has to match the token's stroke-width fallback (2px) or * the clip margin would come up short the moment a skin activates. * * WHY this no longer feeds a drawn line: before * docs/peps/0001-sketch-skin-at-the-boundary.md, this fed `SketchOutline` * directly. The boundary pass now measures its own pen width off * `getComputedStyle(el).borderTopWidth` (`sketchAtEdge.ts`'s `measureBox`), * which is more honest than a duplicated literal — this constant only * has to stay right for the clip allowance, not for two things at once. */ const BLOCK_BORDER_PX = 2; /** * WHY: docs/peps/0001-sketch-skin-at-the-boundary.md M2. Slack for any * decorative child that paints just outside the border box — NOT a skin * import, and not a number the skin gets to set. Before this migration * this was `SKETCH_OUTLINE_BLEED_PX`, imported from the skin because the * in-core `SketchOutline` was that decorative child; the boundary's own * twin is now appended as a child of THIS element (`sketchAtEdge.ts`'s * `upsertBoxTwin`) after this component has already rendered, so the same * clip allowance is still needed, just granted generically rather than * borrowed from the thing that used to need it. Value unchanged: 5, the * same `Math.ceil(SKETCH_WOBBLE_PX + 2)` the donor computed. */ const OUTLINE_BLEED_PX = 5; export function Block({ header, body, footer, width = 320, height, shape = "card", style, showHeaderDivider = true, headerFit = "full", showFooterDivider = true, description, showDescription = true, descriptionSlot, members, membersLayout = "free", onMembersChange, membersReorderChord, memberGap = BLOCK_MEMBER_GAP_PX, memberGutter = BLOCK_MEMBER_INSET_PX, insetBackground = "none", showMembers = true, showCards = false, diagnostics, highlighterKind = DEFAULT_HIGHLIGHTER_KIND, showDiagnosticFlag = true, diagnosticWarningGlow = false, sketchSeed, showHitRegion = false, }: BlockProps) { const diagnosticSeverity = maxDiagnosticSeverity(diagnostics); const markedSeverity = diagnosticSeverity !== "info" ? diagnosticSeverity : undefined; // "Warning must not shout" (§5's own words for this row) is the // "halo" kind's OWN, narrower rule — an error-only escalation by // default, never amber, unless the caller (ValueCapsule) has no other // channel and opts warning in. `stroke`/`mask` mark both severities // uniformly — a crisp outline is not the loud thing "must not shout" // was written about. const showGlow = highlighterKind === "halo" && (markedSeverity === "error" || (markedSeverity === "warning" && diagnosticWarningGlow)); const showStroke = highlighterKind === "stroke" && markedSeverity != null; const showMask = highlighterKind === "mask" && markedSeverity != null; const showFlag = showDiagnosticFlag && markedSeverity != null; // Half the flag's own diameter pokes outside the border — "straddling // the corner the way wall ports straddle walls" (§5). `overflowClipMargin` // below has to widen to let it, exactly the mechanism already in place // for the sketch outline's own bleed (this file's existing WHY on // `overflow: clip`). The "mask" kind renders a SIBLING frame (below) that // pokes out by the same amount for the same reason; "stroke" needs no // widening at all — a CSS `outline` paints outside the border box but is // NOT part of what the element's own `overflow` clips (same rule that // already let the pre-existing glow's box-shadow skip this entirely). const flagOverhangPx = DIAGNOSTIC_FLAG_SIZE_PX / 2; const MASK_OFFSET_PX = 4; const maskOverhangPx = showMask ? MASK_OFFSET_PX : 0; return (

{showMask && markedSeverity && ( // `"mask"` (HighlighterKind's own doc): a sibling frame whose // `border-radius` grows by EXACTLY the offset — the Minkowski-sum // arithmetic that makes this genuinely equidistant at the corners, // unlike `"stroke"`'s plain `outline-offset` above.
)} {showFlag && diagnostics && ( // Straddles the top-right corner — half in, half out — the same // convergence Appendix B's own table names (maxGraph's // `defaultOverlap: 0.5`, JointJS's `Button` at `x:'100%'`, Vyuh's // "-8px offset"). `zIndex` clears the sketch outline's own drawn // stroke, which otherwise paints OVER a flag sitting this close to // the corner.
)} {showHitRegion && (

A bottom-only rule on a narrower tab // would leave the body's top-right corner, past the tab, with // no line at all — which is exactly the "full" header's rule, // not the tab's. showHeaderDivider && (headerFit === "hug" ? /**
 * src/components/hitRegion.ts — the one shared paint for `showHitRegion`.
 *
 * WHY this lives in `components/`, not beside the story harness
 * (`src/hitRegions/`): the components themselves paint their hit regions
 * (a `showHitRegion` prop paints the EXISTING hit element — Port's halo
 * span, Trace's hit path — rather than a second overlay that could drift
 * from the real target), so the paint tokens must be importable from the
 * core side. The harness imports components, never the reverse.
 *
 * WHY the region is painted BY the hit element itself and never by a
 * separate measured overlay: the whole exercise exists to avoid a drawn
 * rectangle that does not correspond to real hit-testing (pyblocks'
 * hit-regions report, 2026-08-27, calls that decoration). Painting the
 * element that IS the pointer target makes region and target identical by
 * construction — they share one DOM node, one geometry, one constant.
 *
 * WHY orange (`--bbox-primary`) and not the Chrome-inspector red that
 * `PortEdge`'s `showCard` uses: red already means "layout slot" in this
 * app's dev overlays. Hit regions are a different fact (where the pointer
 * lands, not where layout reserves space), so they get a different colour
 * — the design system's own accent, translucent enough to read what is
 * under it.
 */

/** Translucent wash for an area-shaped hit region (Port's halo circle,
 * Block's border box, a handle circle). */
export const HIT_REGION_FILL =
  "color-mix(in srgb, var(--bbox-primary, #f0883e) 20%, transparent)";

/** The same wash for a STROKE-shaped hit region (Trace's invisible hit
 * path) — one token, so a band and an area read as the same overlay. */
export const HIT_REGION_STROKE = HIT_REGION_FILL;

/** Edge line for the region, so its boundary is readable even where the
 * wash sits over a busy background. */
export const HIT_REGION_LINE =
  "color-mix(in srgb, var(--bbox-primary, #f0883e) 75%, transparent)";

/** CSS `outline` shorthand — outline never affects layout, which is what
 * keeps `showHitRegion` a pure paint fact (toggling it moves nothing). */
export const HIT_REGION_OUTLINE = `1px dashed ${HIT_REGION_LINE}`;
